top.first_line: Day 1 of the close: what do you check before anything else?
The last week of the month should not belong to spreadsheets.
Our customers close in 5 working days on average. Here is what changed for them.

pattern: The 3 winners all lead with something concrete about the checklist itself: Doc - checklist preview (document) ($81.35 a lead) with what is inside, Checklist - 42 checks (image) ($84.26 a lead) with a number and Checklist - controller quote (image) ($105.12 a lead) with a customer's own words; each first sentence fits in 150 characters.

The losers open on the product or a vague promise: Demo - exceptions only (image) spent $1,980 for no lead, Demo - 30 min walkthrough (image) cost $350.00 a lead and Checklist - new year close (image) $203.33, against a $120 target.

Seniority splits the winners: Checklist - 42 checks (image) is cheapest for Senior and Manager staff, Doc - checklist preview (document) for Directors and Checklist - controller quote (image) for VPs; no winner has 5 leads from CXOs, so that row is too few to call.

The page's top organic opening, "Day 1 of the close: what do you check before anything else?" (4.44% engagement), is a day 1 question, so this round tests question hooks against the winners' instruction and number openings.

checks.detail: single image intros 129 to 140 characters, headlines 30 to 49; document intros 128 to 146; carousel cards 14 to 35 of 45; lead form headlines 33, 37 of 60, details 144 of 160, thank-you 197 of 300; every intro within 150 and every headline within 70
every feed intro's first sentence ends within 150 characters (longest 136)
every number in the copy (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 9, 14, 30, 42) appears in the facts given or the account's own ads
no headline repeats an intro's first sentence, and no two lines in a set differ by two words or fewer
5 message nodes, most buttons 4 of 5, longest button 23 of 25, deepest node 1 click(s) from the opening, 0 dead ends, 0 unreachable nodes
no line names a reader's personal traits, no deadline or scarcity, no jobs, housing or credit offer
